content.intro: This lesson develops topic 174 of the supplied curriculum: **Contiguous and Non-Contiguous Arrays**. The main starting point is **C-contiguous layout**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Views and references can share memory, while copies own separate data. Awareness of this difference prevents accidental mutation and helps explain memory/performance trade-offs.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Contiguous and Non-Contiguous Arrays** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **C-contiguous layout** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
print(a.flags.c_contiguous, a.T.flags.c_contiguous)

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a slice owns independent memory
common_mistakes.why: Basic slicing commonly creates a view.
Short timings vary due to startup, cache, and system noise.
